Section 8.10--Semiannual Assessment for Certain Institutions Section 8.10, as proposed, established the primary assessment for nonbank Federal qualified payment stablecoin issuers, certain foreign payment stablecoin issuers, and State qualified payment stablecoin issuers subject to 12 U.S.C. 5903(d) (except to the extent such issuer remains solely supervised by a State payment stablecoin regulator).\209\ Proposed Sec. 8.10(a) in general incorporated the current structure and asset-based formula used to impose assessments on national banks and Federal savings associations under Sec. 8.2(a), and included the same percentage-based assessment reduction for minimum stablecoin reserve assets that the agency proposed under Sec. 8.2(e)(1), discussed above. Consistent with the agency's treatment of national banks and Federal savings associations, proposed Sec. 8.10(a) imposed a semiannual assessment schedule. In addition to ensuring consistency across all categories of supervised institutions, a semiannual assessment schedule may be especially prudent for those institutions subject to proposed Sec. 8.10, given that stablecoin reserve assets--the primary asset for many of the subject institutions--may experience significant fluctuation over the course of a year as issuance and transaction volumes change. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- \209\ State qualified payment stablecoin issuers with consolidated total outstanding issuances of not more than $10 billion may opt for regulation under a State-level regulatory regime under 12 U.S.C. 5903(c). However, when a State-chartered depository institution that is a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer exceeds a threshold of $10 billion consolidated total outstanding issuance, not later than 360 days after reaching such threshold, it transitions to the Federal regulatory framework of its primary Federal payment stablecoin regulator, which is administered by the State payment stablecoin regulator and the primary Federal payment stablecoin regulator acting jointly. Similarly, when a non- depository State qualified payment stablecoin issuer exceeds a threshold of $10 billion consolidated total outstanding issuance, not later than 360 days after reaching such threshold, it transitions to the Federal regulatory framework of the OCC, administered by the relevant State payment stablecoin regulator and the OCC acting in coordination. This means that some State qualified payment stablecoin issuers will be subject to the OCC's regulatory framework administered by the relevant State payment stablecoin regulator and the OCC acting jointly or in coordination. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- To ensure the annual assessment of an institution subject to proposed Sec. 8.10(a) would be in an amount equal to the annual assessment of a similarly-sized national bank or Federal savings association under Sec. 8.2(a), the OCC proposed to use the same asset tiers (Columns A and B) in Table 1 of [[Page 67149]] Sec. 8.10(a) as used in Table 1 of Sec. 8.2(a),\210\ and to publish in its annual Notices of Fees tier-specific base amounts (Column C) and marginal rates (Column D) that match those published annually in connection with current Sec. 8.2(a).\211\ Proposed Sec. 8.10(a)(6) likewise established the same two-pronged approach to calculating assessments for the on-balance-sheet assets of institutions subject to that section as proposed in Sec. 8.2(e)(1). --------------------------------------------------------------------------- \210\ As discussed elsewhere, the OCC's current asset-based assessment scheme assigns each bank to a bracket based on total assets. For each bracket, the assessment is a base amount (representing application of successive marginal rates to the assets up to the lower threshold of that bracket) plus a marginal rate applied to amounts within that tier. There are currently eleven brackets, the thresholds for which are set by regulation. Current base amounts and marginal rates are published annually in the Notice of Fees. See 57 FR 22413 (May 28, 1992) (discussing overall methodology); 73 FR 9012 (February 19, 2008) (establishing current asset size thresholds). The most recent Notice of Fees can be found on the OCC's website. See, e.g., OCC Bulletin 2025-21, ``Office of the Comptroller of the Currency Fees and Assessments: Interim Calendar Year 2025 Fees and Assessments Structure'' (August 29, 2025), https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2025/bulletin-2025-21.html. \211\ Accordingly, consistent with current Sec. 8.2(a), proposed Sec. 8.10(a)(4) would provide that the OCC may index marginal rates to adjust for the percentage in the level of prices, as measured by changes in the Gross Domestic Product Implicit Price Deflator (GDPIPD) for each June-to-June period. It would similarly reserve for the agency a degree of discretion to adjust marginal rates by amounts other than the percentage change in the GDPIPD. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Specifically, the OCC proposed to use the existing asset-based formula to first determine the institution's semiannual assessment attributable to its on-balance-sheet assets that do not reflect minimum stablecoin reserve assets. As noted, the agency anticipated that institutions subject to proposed Sec. 8.10 will have a limited amount of such assets on balance sheet. The OCC next proposed to apply the same formula to those minimum stablecoin reserve assets, except that it would reduce the resulting amount by 35 percent, or by such other percentage (up to 55 percent) that the OCC may deem appropriate for minimum stablecoin reserves held by institutions subject to proposed Sec. 8.10, based on its experience supervising all stablecoin issuers subject to this part. The OCC would publish the percentage reduction deemed appropriate for minimum stablecoin reserve assets on an annual basis in the Notice of Fees. An institution's semiannual assessment would be the sum of the two figures described above. For the reasons already discussed, the OCC has removed references to foreign payment stablecoin issuers subject to the OCC's jurisdiction. The OCC will calculate assessments for foreign payment stablecoin issuers in the separate manner described above. Whereas proposed Sec. 8.10 applied an assessment discount only to the minimum stablecoin reserve assets required by the GENIUS Act, the final version of Sec. 8.10 parallels the change in the final version of Sec. 8.2 by removing the minimum amount limitation and applying the assessment discount to all stablecoin reserve assets held by the issuer. Consequently, the assessment discount would apply to reserve asset holdings above the minimum. As described in the above discussion of Sec. 8.2, the agency understands reserve asset holdings above the minimum can contribute to reduced overall supervisory risk when it reflects appropriate and conservative risk management decisions, and the agency sees a benefit in encouraging such decisions. Furthermore, the information the agency has learned and expects to receive from stablecoin issuers mitigates the potential risks associated with reserve asset holdings above the minimum, such as asset mischaracterization. Separately, the agency is finalizing the assessment reduction on reserve assets as proposed. Like certain activities of institutions subject to subpart A of part 8, certain GENIUS Act-related activities of institutions subject to subpart B (such as reserve management) are likely to present lower risks and supervisory costs than traditional banking activities. However, given the agency's uncertainty about the complexity of other GENIUS Act-related activities, the agency is not finalizing the reduction above the 35 percent in the proposal. As in the proposal, the agency will review the complexity and supervisory costs associated with GENIUS Act-related activities, which may lead the agency to adjust the assessment reduction as high as 55 percent. The final Sec. 8.10(a)(6)(i) replaces the word ``other'' with ``greater'' to clarify that 35 percent is the lower bound of the range of assessment discounts. The above-described finalization of Sec. 8.10 to apply a 35 percent discount to all stablecoin reserve assets aligns Sec. 8.10 with final Sec. 8.2. As mentioned above, the agency is looking to achieve consistency across categories of supervised institutions to the extent other objectives permit, and applying the same discount between Sec. 8.2 and Sec. 8.10 supports such consistency. Presently, the OCC relies primarily on Call Reports to calculate the total consolidated on-balance-sheet assets of national banks and Federal savings associations for purposes of calculating semiannual assessments under Sec. 8.2(a). Because many institutions subject to proposed Sec. 8.10 do not presently file Call Reports, proposed Sec. 8.10(a)(5) instead provided that the OCC would base semiannual assessments on the total consolidated assets shown on the most recent quarterly report filed by each institution pursuant to proposed Sec. 15.14(i) preceding the payment date. As discussed elsewhere, the OCC proposed to require all institutions subject to proposed Sec. 8.10 to file quarterly reports reflecting the total consolidated assets held on the balance sheet of the institutions. The OCC anticipated that the asset reporting on these quarterly reports will match the asset reporting that would otherwise appear on Call Reports if all institutions subject to proposed Sec. 8.10 were required to file these reports quarterly. The OCC requested comment on the proposed use of weekly or quarterly reporting under Sec. 15.14 to determine the appropriate semiannual assessment amount due from each supervised institution in connection with its GENIUS Act-related activities, including for those institutions subject to subpart B. In particular, the OCC asked whether the agency should require reserve asset reporting on a rolling daily or weekly basis directly to the agency and whether required reporting should focus on the latest figures, the highest figures, the median, or the mean. The OCC received several comments related to this request, some of which it separately addresses in connection with the agency's discussion of Sec. 15.14, as finalized, and the remainder of which are addressed here. One commenter argued that the OCC's assessment methodology should be tied to the reporting regime established in proposed Sec. 15.14 and warned against turning assessments into a reporting regime apart from that contemplated under Sec. 15.14. This commenter also suggested that the OCC rely on the existing weekly reporting under Sec. 15.14(h), arguing that requiring rolling or daily reporting directly to the OCC would be burdensome and not provide clear incremental value relative to the weekly and quarterly reporting. Another commenter opined that the OCC should use the proposed weekly reporting under Sec. 15.14(h) to calculate assessments from a rolling average or other smoothing measure over the assessment period, rather than from only the latest observation. It suggested that while daily reporting should not be mandatory for all issuers, because that would add substantial burden, the OCC should reserve authority to require daily [[Page 67150]] data from large, fast-growing, or stressed issuers. The OCC concludes that quarterly reporting under Sec. 15.14 is adequate and appropriate to calculate assessments. The OCC agrees with commenters that, at least for assessment-related purposes, daily or other reporting directly to the OCC separate and apart from the reporting required under Sec. 15.14 would be unduly burdensome and would not meaningfully impact the OCC's ability to ensure it can fund its activities in connection with the GENIUS Act. The OCC similarly does not believe that rolling averages or other smoothing techniques-- either for purposes of calculating the OCC's jurisdictional thresholds or as a basis for assessments--is necessary for the agency to have actionable and appropriate information to calculate assessments that ensure the agency can fund its activities. Reliance on end-of-quarter reporting of reserve assets is consistent with the agency's current approach to calculating existing asset-based assessments for national banks and Federal savings associations, and the OCC does not expect that reliance on quarterly reporting of reserve assets would meaningfully affect assessment amounts. One commenter requested that the OCC explain further how reporting data will be used to calculate the semiannual assessment base. As noted, unless otherwise indicated, the semiannual assessment of an institution subject to Sec. 8.10(a) will be in an amount equal to the semiannual assessment of a similarly sized national bank or Federal savings association under Sec. 8.2(a). Total balance sheet asset reporting under Sec. 15.14, Schedule B, should provide the OCC with the same or substantially similar balance sheet asset reporting as that provided by similarly situated national banks and Federal savings associations in Call Reports. The OCC will therefore calculate the semiannual assessments under Sec. 8.10(a) using the assets shown on Schedule B of the most recent quarterly report filed by each institution, and relying on the same assessment formula applicable to national banks and Federal savings associations under Sec. 8.2(a), with the reserve asset data provided to the OCC in Schedule B to calculate the reserve asset discount. Section 8.10, as finalized, is revised to better reflect this formula. Finally, similar to proposed amendments in subpart A, proposed Sec. 8.10(a)(6) included language clarifying that the OCC shall increase the assessment set forth in Sec. 8.10(a) for any institution if the assets reported on that institution's quarterly report for any reason do not reflect the minimum stablecoin reserve assets that a stablecoin issuer must hold under 12 U.S.C. 5903 and these implementing regulations. The proposed increase would reflect the difference between the amount of stablecoin reserve assets reflected on the quarterly report and the minimum required stablecoin reserve assets for the amount of outstanding stablecoin issuances that the institution reports. As discussed above, among other things, this proposed subsection would permit the OCC to address any potential under- assessment resulting from an institution's failure to ensure that it holds sufficient stablecoin reserve assets to meet its obligations under 12 U.S.C. 5903 and these implementing regulations. If a stablecoin issuer's actual reserve amount is less than its required reserve amount, the OCC anticipates that the institution may incur additional fees and charges under proposed Sec. 8.12 associated with (among other things) examinations conducted to understand and address the stablecoin issuer's reserve asset deficiencies. While the OCC did not receive comment directly on this provision, the final rule makes certain revisions to ensure overall consistency with similar revisions to subpart A (final Sec. 8.7(d)). Specifically, the final rule provides that, if the assets reported by an institution on its most recent quarterly report preceding the payment date for assessments do not reflect the assets that the institution holds under 12 U.S.C. 5903--or the assets that are otherwise attributable to the institution's custodial and safekeeping activities--the OCC may increase the assessment set forth in subpart B for such institution to fully reflect the appropriate amount of attributable assets. Because the provision would no longer apply solely to reporting inconsistencies in connection with semiannual assessments under Sec. 8.10, the OCC will remove this provision from Sec. 8.10 and add it to proposed Sec. 8.13, ``Payment of interest on delinquent assessments and examination and investigation fees.'' As discussed in connection with similar revisions in subpart A, by expanding the provision to cover all assets attributable to GENIUS Act-related activities subject to assessment-- and not simply minimum reserve assets subject to semiannual assessment under Sec. 8.10--the revised provision best ensures that an institution's assessment amount appropriately reflects the GENIUS Act- related activities of permitted payment stablecoin issuers. The OCC does not anticipate this provision would apply to institutions in the ordinary course. Absent reporting errors or non-compliance with the quarterly reporting forms established under Sec. 15.14, the OCC expects to receive all the information that it will need to assess institutions subject to subpart B solely by reference to Schedules B and C of the institution's quarterly reporting. And, except to the extent a reallocation appears to be the result of misreporting on the part of the institution, the OCC does not intend to treat reallocations under this new subsection as delinquent assessments subject to fees unless and until it has informed the institution of the reassessment and the institution has declined to pay the assessment by the date indicated. Proposed Sec. 8.10(b), modeled after existing Sec. 8.2(d), applied a surcharge to the semiannual assessments for stablecoin issuers that require increased OCC supervisory resources. Similar to the OCC's assessment schedule for national banks and Federal savings associations, the surcharge ensures that fees reflect the increased cost of supervising stablecoin issuers determined to require rehabilitation. As explained above, a condition-based surcharge ensures the OCC has sufficient resources to fund the special supervisory attention that lower-rated entities require without raising general assessments; in the absence of such a charge, healthier entities would in effect subsidize their lower-rated competitors.\212\ The OCC proposed to determine relevant surcharges by multiplying the semiannual assessment computed in accordance with paragraph (a) by 1.5, in the case of any institution that was found to require rehabilitation at its most recent examination; and 2.0 in the case of any institution that was found to have material financial or operational deficiencies that threaten the viability of the institution at its most recent examination prior to December 31 or June 30, as appropriate. This proposed methodology was intended to operate in the same manner, and on the same rationale, as the surcharges tied to UFIRS ratings in Sec. 8.2(d). The OCC generally requested information and comment on its proposed methodology to ensure that assessments for all regulated entities requiring rehabilitation are adequately reflected in the increased cost of supervising those institutions. In Sec. 8.10(b), as finalized, the OCC is changing the language used for purposes of the surcharge to better align with the conditions specified in the surcharges tied to UFIRS ratings in Sec. 8.2(d). Specifically, under the final

was found to be in deficient or critically deficient condition, at its 
most recent examination prior to December 31 or June 30, as 
appropriate.

d. Section 8.11--Fees for Certain Institutions Engaged in the Custodial 
and Safekeeping Activities Permitted Under the GENIUS Act
    Certain institutions subject to assessments under proposed Sec.  
8.10 also would have been subject to an additional assessment under 
proposed Sec.  8.11 in connection with their participation in custodial 
or safekeeping activities permitted under 12 U.S.C. 5901 et seq. 
Specifically, proposed Sec.  8.11 would have applied to those 
institutions for which 50 percent or more of their income is derived 
from custodial or safekeeping activities permitted under 12 U.S.C. 5901

Amendments to Part 19 The OCC proposed several revisions to the rules of practice and procedure for adjudicatory proceedings in 12 CFR part 19 to incorporate the Act's procedural requirements with respect to permitted payment stablecoin issuers. Section 6(b) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5905(b)) requires the OCC to follow certain procedures when bringing an enforcement action or imposing civil money penalties against a permitted payment stablecoin issuer for violations of the GENIUS Act, any regulation or order issued under the Act, or any condition imposed in writing between the OCC and permitted payment stablecoin issuer. Specifically, section 6(b)(4)(A) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5905(b)(4)(A)) requires the OCC to comply with the procedures set forth in paragraphs (b) and (e) of section 8 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act (12 U.S.C. 1818) if the OCC identifies a violation or attempted violation of the Act or makes a determination with respect to the enforcement authorities enumerated at sections 6(b)(1) through (3) of the Act.\214\ Similarly, section 6(b)(4)(D) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5905(b)(4)(D)) permits the OCC to follow the procedures in section 8(c) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act when the OCC issues a temporary cease-and-desist order. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- \214\ Section 6(b)(1) through (3) of the Act provide the OCC authority to suspend or revoke the registration of a permitted payment stablecoin issuer, initiate cease-and-desist proceedings, and remove and prohibit institution-affiliated parties. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Section 6(b)(5)(D) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5905(b)(5)(D)) clarifies that any civil money penalty imposed under the Act may be assessed and collected by the OCC pursuant to the procedures set forth in section 8(i)(2) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. [[Page 67153]] Consistent with the GENIUS Act, the OCC proposed to revise Sec. 19.1 to clarify that the rules of practice and procedure in part 19 apply to the following proceedings: suspension or revocation of registration, cease-and-desist, temporary cease-and-desist, removal and prohibition, or civil money penalties under section 6 of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5905). Specifically, the OCC proposed to revise the definitions of ``institution'' and ``institution-affiliated party'' in Sec. 19.3 to incorporate permitted payment stablecoin issuers and actions brought pursuant to the Act. The OCC received no comments on the proposed revisions to part 19. The OCC is finalizing the revisions to part 19 as proposed other than adding a reference to 12 U.S.C. 5905 in the authority section. III. Effective Date The effective date for the final rule is January 18, 2027. The GENIUS Act will be effective on January 18, 2027, and it is important for the implementing regulations to be effective as of the same date. Although the effective date will not be the first day of the next calendar quarter that begins at least 60 days after the final rule is published in the Federal Register,\215\ the effective date is in the next calendar quarter that begins at least 60 days after the final rule is published in the Federal Register. The final rule cannot be effective until the underlying Act that it is implementing is effective. Congress provided in the GENIUS Act that the Act would take effect the earlier of the date that is 18 months after enactment, which would be January 18, 2027, or the date that is 120 days after the date on which the primary Federal payment stablecoin regulators issue any final regulations. Because this final rule is the first final rule issued by a primary Federal payment stablecoin regulator implementing the Act and 120 days following it would be later than January 18, 2027, January 18, 2027, will be the effective date of the Act. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- \215\ See 12 U.S.C. 4802(b)(1)(C) (providing that new regulations and amendments to regulations that impose certain requirements shall take effect on the first day of a calendar quarter which begins on or after the date on which the regulations are published, unless the regulation is required to take effect on a different date pursuant to an Act of Congress). --------------------------------------------------------------------------- IV. Expected Effects The OCC anticipates that the primary effect of the Act and the final rule would be an increase in the aggregate market capitalization of payment stablecoins in response to an increased demand for payment stablecoins due to greater adoption. While the OCC expects that payment stablecoins would still have been issued in the absence of the GENIUS Act, the OCC anticipates that regulatory clarity and regulatory simplification from the final rule will encourage payment stablecoin issuance in the short run beyond the issuance that would have taken place in the absence of the rule. Consistent with the final rule text, this analysis assumes that permitted payment stablecoin issuers will not pay the holder of a payment stablecoin any form of interest or yield solely in connection with the holding, use, or retention of such payment stablecoin. The analysis below focuses on the increased demand for short-term Treasury debt securities that may follow as a result of the reserve requirements in the rule. Effect on Cost of Short-Term Treasury Debt Financing The OCC anticipates that the final rule will benefit the U.S. government and taxpayers by increasing the demand for short-term Treasury debt securities. The rule may raise demand for short-term Treasuries because it requires stablecoin issuers to back outstanding stablecoins with highly liquid assets, which include short-term U.S. Treasury bills with a maturity of 93 days or less. Because research suggests that short-term Treasury securities do not have close substitutes, an increase in demand for these securities would be expected to lower short-term Treasury yields. Azzimonthi and Quadrini (2024) and Ahmed and Aldasoro (2025) similarly estimate that increased demand for short-term Treasuries arising from stablecoin issuance could have a sizeable impact on short-term Treasury yields and other short-term interest rates.\216\ --------------------------------------------------------------------------- \216\ For instance, Ahmed and Aldasoro (2025) claim that a $3.5 billion inflow into stablecoins could lower three-month Treasury yields by 2 to 2.5 basis points within 10 days. See https://www.bis.org/publ/work1270.pdf. Azzim https://www.bis.org/publ/work1270.pdf. Azzimonti and Quadrini (2024) estimate that widespread use of stablecoins, backed by U.S. securities, could put as much as 40 basis points downward pressure on interest rates. See https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/pandp.20241069. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- The final rule's effect on short-term Treasury yields may also be moderated by external factors. For example, the U.S. Treasury could respond to lower financing costs by increasing short-term debt issuance or the Federal Reserve could sell short-term Treasury securities from its balance sheet. Either response would increase supply and partially offset downward pressure on yields. Overall, the final rule has the potential to lower short-term Treasury financing costs. However, this effect would be offset to the extent that stablecoin reserve demand represents a substitution away from other sources of demand for short-term Treasury securities rather than a net increase in demand. Ultimately, the total effect will be driven by the proposal's net effect on the supply and demand for Treasury debt securities. Finally, these effects should be evaluated relative to the pre- GENIUS Act baseline. Using a post-GENIUS baseline would risk attributing the effects of new stablecoin issuance on Treasury markets to the GENIUS Act rather than the rule. Effect of Demand for Short-Term Debt on Other Short-Term Debt Markets The OCC expects that an increase in demand for short-term Treasury securities resulting from the final rule's reserve requirements could benefit borrowers in short-term debt markets by lowering short-term interest rates overall. This could occur if the reserve requirement increases market demand for short-term government debt, which would put downward pressure on overall short-term market debt yields. For example, the increase in demand for short-term Treasury debt from stablecoin reserve assets could benefit corporate debt issuers by lowering yields on short-term corporate debt issues, potentially raising private sector investment in the economy. The economic reasoning underlying this effect relies on the assumption that debt instruments with different maturities are imperfect substitutes for investors. Under imperfect substitutability, an increase in demand for short-term Treasury securities represents an increase in overall market demand for short-term debt, which lowers the cost of short-term debt financing if other investors bidding for short- term debt do not shift their demand to long-term debt securities in to obtain higher yields. In particular, a study by Greenwood, Hanson, and Stein (2010) suggest that an increase in the supply of short-term Treasury debt would raise the relative cost of short-term debt financing relative to long-term financing if new short-term Treasury debt issuance exhausts [[Page 67154]] additional market demand for short-term debt.\217\ --------------------------------------------------------------------------- \217\ The reference to this study is Greenwood, Hanson, and Stein, A Gap-Filling Theory of Corporate Debt Maturity Choice, Journal of Finance, 2010. --------------------------------------------------------------------------- The OCC expects that an offsetting increase in the demand for short-term Treasury debt to fund stablecoin reserves would neutralize the effect of short-term Treasury debt issuance on the market cost of short-term debt financing as described by Greenwood, Hanson, and Stein (2010). This is because an increase in the demand for short-term Treasury debt from stablecoin reserves would consume some fraction of the additional supply of Treasury debt. Therefore, the OCC expects that, if the rule's reserve requirements increase the demand for short-term Treasury debt, this could increase the overall market demand for short-term debt and lower the cost of short-term debt for other borrowers, such as short-term corporate debt issuers. Title: Reporting, Recordkeeping, and Disclosure Requirements Associated with the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act for the Issuance of Stablecoins by Entities Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. OMB Control No.: 1557-NEW. Type of Review: Regular. Affected Public: Businesses or other for-profit. Description: Twelve CFR part 15 sets forth the OCC's Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (12 U.S.C. 5901 et seq.) regarding the issuance of payment stablecoins and certain related activities by entities subject to the OCC's jurisdiction. The information collection requirements in the rule are as follows: Reporting Requirements Section 15.10(c) sets forth prohibitions that apply to permitted payment stablecoin issuers, including a prohibition on paying interest or yield to payment stablecoin holders solely in connection with the holding, use, or retention of a payment stablecoin and a general prohibition against pledging, rehypothecating, or reusing reserve assets. Section 15.10(c)(5)(iii)(B) permits creating liquidity to meet reasonable expectations of requests to redeem payment stablecoins, such that reserves in the form of Treasury bills with a maturity of 93 days or less may be sold as purchased securities in repurchase agreements, after receiving the prior approval from the OCC, notwithstanding a general prohibition against pledging, rehypothecating, or reusing reserve assets. Section 15.11(a)(2) requires permitted payment stablecoin issuers to demonstrate the operational capability to access and monetize the identifiable reserve assets to meet redemptions, in both normal and adverse economic, liquidity, market, and interest rate conditions, commensurate with the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's risk profile and business model, taking into account, among other relevant factors, market access, financing channels, haircut assumptions, and operational readiness. Section 15.11(e) sets forth specific instructions for composition reports, including their preparation requirements. Under Sec. 15.11(e)(2) the composition report is required to use a format like the template provided in Table 1 of Sec. 15.11(e) and contain the total number of outstanding payment stablecoins issued by the issuer and the amount and composition of the reserves described in Sec. 15.11(a), including the average tenor and geographic location of custody of each category of reserve instruments. Section 15.11(g)(1) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to notify the OCC, through its OCC supervisory office, on any day in which its reserve asset amount has fallen below the minimum reserve asset amount required by Sec. 15.11(a). Under Sec. 15.11(g)(4)(i), if the OCC determines that a permitted payment stablecoin issuer has not demonstrated that it meets the requirements of Sec. 15.11(a), (b), (c), or (d), the OCC may require the issuer to submit a plan describing how the permitted payment stablecoin issuer will attain compliance and the timeline for the plan. Section 15.12(d)(1) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to provide notice to the OCC within 24 hours if it receives redemption requests in excess of 10 percent of the outstanding issuance value of any brand of payment stablecoin issued by the permitted payment stablecoin issuer in a single 24-hour period. Under Sec. 15.12(d)(2) a permitted payment stablecoin issuer that experiences redemption requests in excess of 10 percent of the outstanding issuance value of any brand of payment stablecoin issued by the permitted payment stablecoin issuer in a single 24-hour period may request that the OCC extend the timeframe for timely redemption. Section 15.13(a)(3)(i) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to manage interest rate risk in a manner that is appropriate to the size and complexity of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer and the complexity of its assets and liabilities. Section 15.13(a)(3)(ii) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to provide for periodic reporting to management and the board of directors regarding interest rate risk with information sufficient for management and the board of directors to assess, to an extent commensurate with their duties, the level of risk. Section 15.13(a)(9) provides monetization and stress testing requirements. Under section 15.13(a)(9)(i) a permitted payment stablecoin issuer is required to conduct analyses that consider a range of redemption scenarios to ensure that the reserve asset portfolio, taken as a whole, is capable of supporting timely redemption under both normal and stressed conditions. Section 15.13(a)(9)(ii) further requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer maintain and demonstrate to the OCC the ability to reliably access and monetize reserve assets necessary to meet redemption requests in normal and stressed conditions, taking into account: market access; financing channels; haircut assumptions; and operational readiness. Finally, Sec. 15.13(a)(9)(iii) requires permitted payment stablecoin issuers to engage in regular stress testing of the reserve asset portfolio in order to determine whether the portfolio of reserve assets will continue to equal or exceed outstanding issuance value in stressed conditions, including in significant positive interest rate scenarios. Section 15.13(a)(10) covers foreign exchange risk. Section 15.13(a)(10)(iii) requires, before engaging in foreign exchange risk management, that the permitted payment stablecoin issuer

[[Page 67155]] provide prior notice to the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's supervisory office and receive the OCC's approval. Section 15.13(b)(7) sets forth notification of unauthorized access requirements that apply to permitted payment stablecoin issuers. Section 15.13(b)(7)(i)(A) requires, when a permitted payment stablecoin issuer becomes aware of an incident of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information, including a customer's private key, the permitted payment stablecoin issuer must conduct a reasonable investigation. Under Sec. 15.13(b)(7)(i)(B) if the permitted payment stablecoin issuer determines that misuse of its information about a customer has occurred or is reasonably possible to occur, notification to the affected or possibly affected customer and the OCC is required as soon as possible. Customer notice must be delayed if an appropriate law enforcement agency determines that notification will interfere with a criminal investigation and the law enforcement agency provides the permitted payment stablecoin issuer with a written request for the delay. Section 15.13(b)(7)(i)(C) requires the permitted payment stablecoin issuer to notify its customers of the misuse or possible misuse of customer information as soon as the law enforcement agency notifies the permitted payment stablecoin issuer that notification will no longer interfere with the investigation. Under Sec. 15.13(b)(7)(ii), if a permitted payment stablecoin issuer determines that the files of a group of customers have been accessed improperly but is unable to identify which specific customers' information has been accessed and if the circumstances of the unauthorized access lead the permitted payment stablecoin issuer to determine that misuse of the information is reasonably possible, it must notify all customers in the group. Section 15.14(h) requires all permitted payment stablecoin issuers to submit to the OCC, on a weekly basis, in the manner and form specified by the OCC, a confidential report containing the information requested in the form available at www.occ.gov. Section 15.14(i) covers the quarterly reports of financial condition and its required contents. Under Sec. 15.14(i)(1), all permitted payment stablecoin issuers subject to OCC supervision are required to submit to the OCC a quarterly report on the financial condition of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer, including, but not limited to, income statement, expenses, balance sheet, reserves, changes in equity, investments, capital, outstanding issuance value, and assets under custody, in a standardized format as prescribed by the OCC and within 30 days of the end of the prior quarter. The forms and instructions are available at www.occ.gov. Under Sec. 15.14(i)(2), each report of financial condition is required to contain a declaration by the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's Chief Financial Officer, or the individual performing an equivalent function, that the report is true and correct to the best of their knowledge and belief. Under Sec. 15.14(i)(3), the correctness of the report of financial condition is required to be attested to by the signatures of the directors and senior management of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer other than the officer, or the individual performing an equivalent function, making such declaration, with the attestation stating that the report has been examined by them and, to the best of their knowledge and belief, is true and correct. Section 15.14(j) covers the submission of other reports requested by the OCC. Upon request, all permitted payment stablecoin issuers are required to submit to the OCC a report on the financial condition of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer; the systems of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer for monitoring and controlling financial and operational risks; compliance of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer and any subsidiary thereof with the GENIUS Act, and 12 CFR part 15; and in the case of a Federal qualified nonbank payment stablecoin issuer, compliance of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer with the requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act and with laws authorizing the imposition of sanctions and implemented by the Secretary of the Treasury. Section 15.14(k) sets forth ongoing compliance reporting. Section 15.14(k)(1) provides that no later than 180 days after the approval of an application, as set forth in Sec. 15.30, and on an annual basis thereafter, a permitted payment stablecoin issuer subject to OCC supervision is required to submit to the OCC a certification that the permitted payment stablecoin issuer has implemented anti-money laundering and economic sanctions compliance programs. The programs are required to be reasonably designed to prevent the permitted payment stablecoin issuer from facilitating money laundering, specifically, facilitating money laundering for cartels and organizations designated as foreign terrorist organizations under section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1189) and the financing of terrorist activities, consistent with the requirements of the GENIUS Act. Section 15.14(k)(2) additionally requires that the initial certification be provided by the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's board of directors. Subsequent certifications may be provided by the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's Bank Secrecy Act officer, the board of directors, or an appropriate committee of the board of directors. Section 15.14(l) sets forth audit requirements and requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer with more than $50 billion in total consolidated outstanding issuance value, that is not subject to certain reporting requirements under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, prepare, in accordance with GAAP, an annual financial statement. Section 15.14(l)(2) sets forth the requirements for preparing and submitting the audited annual financial statements. Section 15.14(l)(2)(ii) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to submit the audited financial statements annually, within 120 days after the end of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's fiscal year, to the OCC. Section 15.14(l)(2)(iii) provides that if a permitted payment stablecoin issuer is unable to timely file all or any portion of the audited annual financial statement required under Sec. 15.14(l)(2)(ii), it must submit a written notice of late filing to the OCC. The notice is required to disclose the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's inability to timely file all, or specified portions, of its annual financial statement and the reasons therefore in reasonable detail; include the date by which the financial statement will be filed; and be filed on or before the deadline for filing the financial statement. Section 15.14(m) sets forth notice requirements for changes in control of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer. Under this section, a person seeking to acquire control of a permitted payment stablecoin issuer is required to follow the requirements of 12 CFR 5.50 as if the permitted payment stablecoin issuer were a national bank. Section 15.15(b)(2) sets forth initial notice requirements for State qualified payment stablecoin issuers that are nonbank entities with a total consolidated outstanding issuance value of more than $10 billion. Under the section, a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer with a total consolidated outstanding issuance value of more than $10 billion is required to provide written notification to the OCC within five calendar days after reaching such threshold. The written notification [[Page 67156]] is required to include: the State or States that currently regulate the State qualified payment stablecoin issuer; the State qualified payment stablecoin issuer's outstanding issuance value as of the date of the notice; the date that the State qualified payment stablecoin issuer first reached the $10 billion total consolidated outstanding issuance value threshold; and an indication of whether and when the State qualified payment stablecoin issuer ceased issuing, on a net basis, new payment stablecoins and whether the State qualified payment stablecoin issuer intends to seek a waiver pursuant to Sec. 15.15(d). Section 15.15(b)(3) sets forth the capital analysis requirements for State qualified payment stablecoin issuers. Under the section, within 270 days of reaching the $10 billion total consolidated outstanding issuance value threshold, a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer is required to submit a capital analysis to the OCC. The analysis is required to include an analysis of the issuer's current capital position and anticipated capital needs, sufficient to ensure ongoing operations, based on its business model and risk profile. A State qualified payment stablecoin issuer is not required to submit a capital analysis if the issuer has received a waiver pursuant to Sec. 15.15(d) or is not required to transition to the Federal regulatory framework pursuant to Sec. 15.15(b)(1)(ii). Section 15.15(b)(4) sets forth compliance notice requirements for a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer. Under Sec. 15.15(b)(4)(i), for purposes of complying with Sec. 15.15(b)(1)(i), a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer is required to provide written notification to the OCC that it complies with the Federal regulatory framework under 12 CFR part 15 or, if the State qualified payment stablecoin issuer is not in compliance with the Federal regulatory framework under 12 CFR part 15, to provide written notice identifying the provisions with which the issuer does not comply, providing the issuer's plan for remediating its noncompliance, and explaining why the issuer did not comply with the Federal regulatory framework within the 360-day transition period. Under Sec. 15.15(b)(4)(ii) a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer that does not cease issuing new payment stablecoins in accordance with Sec. 15.15(b)(1)(ii) is required to transition to the regulatory framework under 12 CFR part 15 on the earlier of 360 days after reaching the $10 billion total consolidated outstanding issuance value threshold or the date on which the State qualified payment stablecoin issuer provides written notification under paragraph (b)(4)(i) of this section. Section 15.15(d)(1)(i) requires a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer seeking to remain solely supervised by a State payment stablecoin regulator to submit to the OCC a written waiver request containing information necessary to evaluate such request under Sec. Sec. 15.15(d)(2) and (3). In addition, Sec. 15.15(d)(1)(ii) provides that a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer seeking to remain solely supervised by a State payment stablecoin regulator is required to submit a waiver request within 240 days of reaching the $10 billion total consolidated outstanding issuance value threshold. Section 15.30(a)(1) sets forth application requirements for insured national banks, Federal savings associations, and insured Federal branches. This section provides that any insured national bank, Federal savings association, or insured Federal branch that seeks to issue payment stablecoins through a subsidiary is required to file an application under this section and receive prior approval from the OCC before the subsidiary may issue payment stablecoins. Section 15.30(a)(2) sets forth application requirements for nonbank entities, uninsured national banks, and uninsured Federal branches. This section provides that any nonbank entity, uninsured national bank, or uninsured Federal branch that seeks to issue payment stablecoins as a Federal qualified payment stablecoin issuer is required to file an application under this section and receive prior approval from the OCC before issuing payment stablecoins. Section 15.30(b) sets forth the application process for insured national banks, Federal savings associations, insured Federal branches and nonbank entities, uninsured national banks, and uninsured Federal branches that seek to issue payment stablecoins. The process would require an applicant to submit all the information required by the form for an application under this section. The forms and instructions are available on the OCC's website. Each director, executive officer, and principal shareholder of the applicant (or in the case of an applicant that is an insured national bank, Federal savings association, or insured Federal branch, of the subsidiary of the applicant) is required to submit the information prescribed in the Interagency Biographical and Financial Report and Corporate Background and Financial Report,\218\ available at the OCC's website. An applicant is required to certify that any filing or supporting material submitted to the OCC contains no material misrepresentations or omissions. An applicant is also required to certify whether section 4(a)(12) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5903(a)(12)) applies to the applicant. The process provides that an applicant should address an application under this section to the appropriate OCC licensing office, unless the OCC advises an applicant otherwise. The OCC will consider an application substantially complete if it contains sufficient information for the OCC to render a decision on whether the applicant satisfies the factors set forth in Sec. 15.30(d). The OCC will notify applicants not later than 30 days after receipt of an application whether the application is substantially complete. If the application is not substantially complete, the OCC will notify the applicant of the information required in order for the application to be substantially complete. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Section 15.30(f) sets forth the OCC's appeal process following the 
agency's denial of a substantially complete application. Section 
15.30(f)(1) provides that an applicant may request a hearing to appeal 
the OCC's denial of a substantially complete application within 30 days 
of receipt of the OCC's notice of denial. The request for a hearing is 
required to be in writing. The applicant may request the hearing be on 
the written record, oral testimony and oral argument, or both. Section 
15.30(f)(3) further provides that if filing a written appeal, the 
applicant must submit in writing all documents and arguments that the 
applicant wishes to be considered.
    Section 15.30(g)(1) provides that an insured national bank, Federal 
savings association, or insured Federal branch that has a pending 
substantially complete application for a subsidiary to become a 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer may request that the OCC waive the 
requirements of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5901 et seq.) or part 15 with 
respect to that subsidiary. The requests are required to be in writing.
    Section 15.30(g)(2) provides that a nonbank entity, uninsured 
national bank, or uninsured Federal branch that has a pending 
substantially complete application to become a Federal qualified 
payment stablecoin issuer may request that the OCC waive the

[[Page 67157]]

requirements of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5901 et seq.) or part 15 with 
respect to that entity. The requests are required to be in writing.
    Section 15.31(a) provides that a foreign payment stablecoin issuer 
is not subject to the prohibitions of section 3 of the GENIUS Act (12 
U.S.C. 5902) if it meets all the requirements provided in the 
paragraph. Section 15.31(a)(3)(ii)(D)(1) provides, as a condition of 
one of several methods of complying with Sec.  15.31(a)(3)(i), a 
requirement for a foreign payment stablecoin issuer to submit for the 
OCC's prior approval a detailed proposal to meet the requirements of 
Sec.  15.31(a)(3)(i).
    Section 15.31(b)(2) sets forth reporting requirements for foreign 
payment stablecoin issuers registered with the OCC. Section 
15.31(b)(2)(i) provides that a foreign payment stablecoin issuer 
registered with the OCC pursuant to Sec.  15.32 is required to produce 
the reports required of a permitted payment stablecoin issuer under 
Sec.  15.14 as well as any other reports the OCC may require. Section 
15.31(b)(2)(ii) further provides that a foreign payment stablecoin 
issuer may request, in writing, an exemption from any reporting 
requirement that would otherwise apply under Sec.  15.14. The OCC may 
grant an exemption in its sole discretion.
    Section 15.32(a) sets forth application requirements for a foreign 
payment stablecoin issuer. This section provides that a foreign payment 
stablecoin issuer that seeks to be registered with the OCC under 
section 18(c) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5916(c)) is required to file 
an application under this section.
    Section 15.32(b) sets forth the application process for a foreign 
payment stablecoin issuer that seeks to be registered with the OCC 
under section 18(c) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5916(c)). The process 
requires an applicant to provide all the information required by the 
form for an application under this section; evidence that the Secretary 
of the Treasury has determined that the applicant is subject to a 
regulatory and supervisory regime comparable to the GENIUS Act with 
respect to payment stablecoins, under section 18 of the GENIUS Act (12 
U.S.C. 5916); a certification that the applicant will make available to 
the OCC all information that the OCC deems necessary to determine and 
enforce compliance with the GENIUS Act and 12 CFR part 15; the 
applicant's consent to United States jurisdiction relating to 
enforcement of the GENIUS Act and 12 CFR part 15; certification that 
any filing or supporting material submitted to the OCC contains no 
material misrepresentations or omissions; and certification as to the 
applicability of section 4(a)(12) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 
5903(a)(12)). The process provides that an applicant should address an 
application under this section to the appropriate OCC licensing office, 
unless the OCC advises an applicant otherwise. The forms and 
instructions will be available on the OCC's website.
    Section 15.32(e) sets forth the conditions of approval for foreign 
payment stablecoin issuers seeking to be registered with the OCC under 
section 18(c) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5916(c)). Section 
15.32(e)(3)(i) requires a foreign payment stablecoin issuer to provide 
evidence that it complies with Sec.  15.31(a) by providing to the OCC, 
by noon on the last day of each month, a report describing the total 
number of outstanding payment stablecoins issued by the foreign payment 
stablecoin issuer held by United States customers and the amount and 
composition of the foreign payment stablecoin issuer's reserves, 
including their geographic location and average tenor of reserve 
instruments. Additionally, Sec.  15.32(e)(3)(ii) requires the report to 
use a format like the template provided in Table 1 to Sec.  
15.32(e)(3)(ii). Section 15.32(e)(3)(iii) requires the foreign payment 
stablecoin issuer to promptly notify the OCC through its supervisory 
office on any day in which the issuer fails to meet the reserve asset 
requirements of Sec.  15.32(e)(3).
    Section 15.32(g) sets forth the OCC's appeal of rejection processes 
for foreign payment stablecoin issuers. A foreign payment stablecoin 
issuer may request a hearing to appeal the OCC's rejection of an 
application for registration within 30 days of receipt of the OCC's 
notice of rejection. Section 15.32(g)(2) requires the request for a 
written or oral hearing to be in writing. Under Sec.  15.32(g)(3), the 
foreign payment stablecoin issuer may request the hearing be on the 
written record, oral testimony and oral argument, or both. Section 
15.32(g)(5) further provides that if filing a written appeal, the 
foreign payment stablecoin issuer must submit in writing all documents 
and arguments that the applicant wishes to be considered.
    Section 15.40(c) describes operational backstop debt which may 
consist of debt instruments in an amount that in total does not exceed 
50 percent of the operational backstop requirement in Sec.  15.41(b) 
and where each debt instrument meets specific criteria. Under Sec.  
15.40(c)(5), a debt instrument may be callable by its terms only after 
a minimum of five years after issuance and only with prior approval of 
the OCC. In addition, the permitted payment stablecoin issuer is 
required to either replace the instrument to be called with an 
equivalent amount of a new instrument meeting the criteria for 
operational backstop debt or demonstrate to the OCC that the permitted 
payment stablecoin issuer has sufficient capital to meet its minimum 
capital requirement in Sec.  15.41.
    Section 15.41 sets forth minimum capital and backstop requirements 
for permitted payment stablecoin issuers. Section 15.41(b)(1)(iii) 
provides that a permitted payment stablecoin issuer may exclude one-
time expenses that are wholly unrelated to the continuing operation of 
the permitted payment stablecoin issuer from the calculation under 
Sec. Sec.  15.41(b)(1)(i) or (ii) with prior written approval of the 
OCC.
    Section 15.41(c)(1)(i) requires a permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer to notify the OCC within 24 hours if it fails to meet either the 
minimum capital or backstop requirement during a quarter. Section 
15.41(c)(1)(ii) further instructs a permitted payment stablecoin issuer 
to publicly report whether it has complied with the minimum capital and 
backstop requirements during the quarter on the report required under 
Sec.  15.14.\219\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \219\ Reporting burden is covered under section 15.14(i).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Section 15.41(d) sets forth uninsured national trust banks' minimum 
capital requirements. Under Sec.  15.41(d)(1), an uninsured national 
trust bank, whether or not it is a permitted payment stablecoin issuer, 
may elect to comply with all of the requirements in Sec. Sec.  15.40 
through 15.42 in lieu of complying with the requirements in 12 CFR part 
3 upon receipt of the OCC's prior approval. Section 15.41(d)(2) 
instructs that, to make the election described in Sec.  15.41(d)(1), an 
uninsured national trust bank must submit a written request for prior 
approval to the appropriate OCC supervisory office, along with 
documentation sufficient to support the bank's minimum capital and 
operational backstop amounts. Section 15.41(d)(4) further provides that 
an uninsured national trust bank may rescind an approved election under 
Sec.  15.41(d) by submitting a notice to the appropriate OCC 
supervisory office.
    Section 15.42 sets forth individual additional capital or 
operational backstop requirements for permitted payment stablecoin 
issuers. Section 15.42(c)(2)(i) provides that a permitted payment 
stablecoin issuer may respond to any or all of the items in the notice 
sent by the OCC notifying the permitted payment stablecoin issuer in 
writing of the proposed additional capital or

[[Page 67158]]

backstop requirement and the date by which it should be reached (if 
applicable). The response is required to be in writing and delivered to 
the OCC within 30 days after the date on which the permitted payment 
stablecoin issuer received the notice or such other time period as the 
OCC determines appropriate based on the condition of the permitted 
payment stablecoin issuer.
    Section 15.42(c)(3) sets forth the OCC's decision process in 
determining whether the individual additional capital or backstop 
requirement should be established for a permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer and, if so, the requirement and the date the requirement will 
become effective. Section 15.42(c)(4) provides that the OCC's decision 
may require the permitted payment stablecoin issuer to develop and 
submit to the OCC, within a time period specified, an acceptable plan 
to reach the additional capital or backstop requirement established for 
the permitted payment stablecoin issuer by the date required.
Recordkeeping Requirements
    Section 15.11(a)(1) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer 
to maintain reserve assets that are identifiable, are segregated from 
and not commingled with other assets owned or held by the permitted 
payment stablecoin issuer, at all times have a reserve asset value that 
equals or exceeds the outstanding issuance value of the permitted 
payment stablecoin issuer, and are either held directly by the 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer or within the custody of an 
eligible financial institution.
    Section 15.11(f)(1) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer 
to, each month, have the information disclosed in the previous month-
end report required under Sec.  15.11(e) examined by a registered 
public accounting firm. Section 15.11(f)(2) requires that each month, 
the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer (or the persons 
performing the equivalent functions) of a permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer submit to the OCC a certification that the monthly report 
required under Sec.  15.11(e) is accurate.
    Section 15.12(c) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer's 
redemption policy to provide clear and conspicuous procedures for 
timely redemption of outstanding payment stablecoins. Timely redemption 
may not exceed two business days following the date of the requested 
redemption and any discretionary limitations on timely redemptions can 
only be imposed by the OCC or, in the case of a State qualified payment 
stablecoin issuer, by the OCC, Board, or the State payment stablecoin 
regulator, as applicable.
    Section 15.13(a)(1) covers internal controls and information 
systems. A permitted payment stablecoin issuer is required to have 
internal controls and information systems to support effective risk 
management that are appropriate for the size and complexity of the 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer and the nature, scope, and risk of 
its activities. The internal controls are required to provide for: an 
organizational structure that establishes clear lines of authority and 
responsibility for monitoring adherence to established policies, 
including appropriate segregation of duties and dual controls; 
effective risk assessment; timely and accurate financial, operational, 
and regulatory reporting, including with respect to the reports 
required under 12 CFR part 15; adequate procedures to monitor, 
safeguard, manage, control, and monetize assets, including reserve 
assets; and compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
    Section 15.13(a)(2) covers internal audit systems. A permitted 
payment stablecoin issuer is required to have an internal audit system 
that is appropriate to the size and complexity of the permitted payment 
stablecoin issuer and the nature, scope, and risk of its activities. 
The internal audit system is required to provide for adequate 
monitoring of the system of internal controls through an internal audit 
function or if the size, complexity, or scope of operations of the 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer does not warrant a full-scale 
internal audit function, a system of independent reviews of key 
internal controls. Additionally, the internal audit system is required 
to provide: independence and objectivity; qualified persons responsible 
for the audit function; and adequate independent testing and review of 
internal controls and information systems, verification of published 
information available to customers, calculations for required reserves, 
and regulatory filings. The internal audit system must also provide for 
adequate documentation of tests and findings and any corrective 
actions; verification and review of management actions to address 
deficiencies; and review by the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's 
audit committee or board of directors of the effectiveness of the 
internal audit systems.
    Section 15.13(a)(5) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer 
to establish and maintain a system that is commensurate with the 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer's size and complexity and the 
nature and scope of its operations to evaluate and monitor earnings and 
ensure that earnings are sufficient to support operations and maintain 
the capital levels required by subpart E of 12 CFR part 15.
    Section 15.13(a)(6)(i)(D) requires that a permitted payment 
stablecoin issuer ensure that transactions between the permitted 
payment stablecoin issuer and insiders or affiliates alone, or in the 
aggregate, are appropriately documented and reviewed by the board of 
directors.
    Section 15.13(a)(10)(ii)(D) requires a permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer to have in place policies and procedures that appropriately 
manage its foreign exchange risk and any attendant risks, including 
risks related to the posting or collection of margin, foreign exchange 
counterparties, and basis risk. The policies and procedures must 
include adherence to Sec. Sec.  15.13(a)(10)(iii) and (iv).
    Section 15.13(b) covers information technology and security 
programs. Section 15.13(b)(1) requires a permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer to implement a comprehensive written information security risk 
and control framework, including a program that assesses and manages 
information technology and information security risks. Section 
15.13(b)(2) requires the board of directors or an appropriate board 
committee to approve the information technology and security program 
and oversee the development, implementation, and maintenance of the 
program, including the appointment of a qualified individual 
responsible for the program. Such oversight includes assigning specific 
responsibility for program implementation and review of program-related 
reports. Section 15.13(b)(3) requires a permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer's information technology and security program include: an 
inventory and classification of assets, processes, and sensitivity of 
data; controls supporting and safeguarding sensitive information and 
processes; evaluation, validation, and reporting processes to ensure 
that key information technology systems and controls, including smart 
contracts, are operating as intended; periodic independent testing; and 
a comprehensive and effective incident identification and assessment 
process and incident response program. Section 15.13(b)(4) requires 
that a permitted payment stablecoin issuer's information technology and 
security program includes administrative, technical, and physical 
safeguards designed to ensure the security and confidentiality of 
records containing nonpublic personal

[[Page 67159]]

information about a customer or sensitive customer information. The 
program must also protect against any anticipated threats or hazards to 
the security or integrity of such records, protect against unauthorized 
access to or use of such records that could result in substantial harm 
or inconvenience to any customer, and to ensure the proper disposal of 
such records. Section 15.13(b)(6)(i) provides that a permitted payment 
stablecoin issuer must monitor any relevant changes in technology, the 
sensitivity of its customer information, internal or external threats, 
and the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's own changing business 
arrangements, such as mergers and acquisitions, alliances and joint 
ventures, third-party arrangements, and changes to applicable 
information systems. Under Sec.  15.13(b)(6)(ii), a permitted payment 
stablecoin issuer is required to evaluate and adjust its information 
technology and security program, as appropriate, based on the 
monitoring required by Sec.  15.13(b)(6)(i). Finally, Sec.  15.13(b)(8) 
requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer's information technology 
and security program include measures to ensure continuity of 
operations and recovery of critical functions, including by conducting 
business impact analyses, testing for vulnerabilities, and testing with 
critical service providers.
    Section 15.13(b)(5) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer 
to develop, implement, and maintain appropriate measures to ensure 
secure handling of digital assets, including private key management, 
backup, and recovery incorporating: (i) relevant technical, 
operational, strategic, market, legal, and compliance considerations 
relating to each digital asset and its underlying ledger; and (ii) 
material developments specifically related to supported digital assets 
and their underlying ledgers.\220\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \220\ If a permitted payment stablecoin issuer holds digital 
assets on a customer's behalf, the permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer's risk management practices must reflect this activity. 
Consistent with the July 14, 2025 Joint Statement on Risk-Management 
Considerations for Crypto-Asset Safekeeping, permitted payment 
stablecoin issuers holding digital assets on a customer's behalf 
would be required to maintain risk management practices, and 
information security practices in particular, that reflect a 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer's capacity to understand a 
complex and evolving asset class, ability to ensure a strong control 
environment, and appropriate contingency plans to address 
unanticipated challenges in effectively providing services to 
customers.

    Section 15.14(f) requires all permitted payment stablecoin issuers 
to maintain a complete set of books and records in English.
    Section 15.14(g) requires all permitted payment stablecoin issuers 
to develop and implement a records retention policy that ensures the 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer can demonstrate compliance with the 
GENIUS Act, 12 CFR part 15, and all applicable laws and regulations.
    Section 15.14(l)(1) requires a registered public accounting firm to 
perform an audit of the financial statements described in Sec.  
15.14(l) and sets forth the auditing requirements.
    Section 15.15(b) covers the requirements related to a State 
qualified payment stablecoin issuer that is a nonbank entity 
transitioning to the OCC's regulatory framework pursuant to section 4 
of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5903). Sections 15.15(b)(1)(i) and (ii) 
require a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer with a total 
consolidated outstanding issuance value of more than $10 billion to no 
later than 360 days after reaching such threshold, transition to the 
Federal regulatory framework under 12 CFR part 15 and comply with the 
provisions of this part applicable to Federal qualified payment 
stablecoin issuers or cease issuing, on a net basis, new payment 
stablecoins until the issuer is under the $10 billion total 
consolidated outstanding issuance value threshold. Additionally, Sec.  
15.15(b)(4)(ii) provides that a State qualified payment stablecoin 
issuer that does not cease issuing new payment stablecoins in 
accordance with Sec.  15.15(b)(1)(ii) would be required to transition 
to the regulatory framework under this part on the earlier of 360 days 
after reaching the $10 billion outstanding issuance value threshold or 
the date on which the State qualified payment stablecoin issuer 
provides written notification under Sec.  15.15(b)(4)(i).
    Section 15.21 sets forth covered asset custodial property 
requirements. Section 15.21(b)(1) provides that a covered custodian is 
required to take appropriate steps to protect the covered assets of 
covered customers from the claims of creditors of the covered custodian 
and any sub-custodian, as applicable, through adopting, implementing, 
and maintaining written custody agreements and policies, procedures, 
and internal controls that are adequate to comply with applicable law 
and that are commensurate with the covered custodian's size, 
complexity, and risk profile and with the nature of the applicable 
covered assets for which it provides custodial services or safekeeping 
services. Section 15.21(b)(2)(i) further provides that a covered 
custodian may maintain the covered assets of a covered customer through 
the use of a sub-custodian if consistent with applicable law, provided 
that the covered custodian maintains adequate safeguards and internal 
controls reasonably designed to provide the covered custodian with 
oversight of the sub-custodian's compliance with the requirements of 12 
CFR part 15, subpart C.
    Section 15.22 sets forth the use of omnibus accounts. Under Sec.  
15.22(c), a sub-custodian may, for convenience, commingle the covered 
custodian's assets with the covered assets of its covered customers in 
one or more omnibus accounts of the sub-custodian; provided that the 
covered custodian maintains adequate safeguards and internal controls 
reasonably designed to ensure that the sub-custodian segregates all 
covered assets of the covered custodian's covered customers from, and 
does not commingle such covered assets with, the assets of the sub-
custodian.
    Section 15.41(a)(2)(ii) requires a permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer to have a process for assessing its overall capital adequacy in 
relation to its business model and risk profile and a comprehensive 
strategy for sustaining an appropriate level of capital to maintain 
ongoing operations.
    Section 15.41(c)(5) provides that among other criteria, the OCC may 
permit a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to continue operations 
while its operational backstop is below the required amount, if the 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer provides a plan within seven days 
to regain compliance with the operational backstop requirement within 
90 days, and the OCC deems the plan viable.
Disclosure Requirements
    Section 15.11(e) sets forth the specific disclosure requirements 
for composition reports. Section 15.11(e)(1) requires a permitted 
payment stablecoin issuer by noon on the last day of each month, to 
publish on the website of the issuer the monthly composition of the 
issuer's reserves held pursuant to the GENIUS Act as of noon on the 
last day of the previous month.
    Section 15.12(b) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to 
publicly disclose its redemption policy and include: the timeframe in 
which the issuer will redeem payment stablecoins and the timeframe 
under which the issuer is required to redeem payment stablecoins under 
Sec.  15.12(c)(1)(i); a statement explaining the limitation in Sec.  
15.12(c)(1)(ii); a statement explaining the scenarios under which the 
redemption period may be extended as described in Sec.  15.12(d); a 
statement with clear instructions on how a payment stablecoin holder 
can redeem a payment stablecoin, including a link to the

[[Page 67160]]

website(s) where a payment stablecoin holder can redeem the payment 
stablecoin; and the minimum number of payment stablecoins, if any, that 
the permitted payment stablecoin issuer will redeem, provided that the 
issuer must redeem any number greater than or equal to one payment 
stablecoin, subject to appropriate customer screening and onboarding.
    Section 15.12(e) sets forth purchase and redemption disclosures and 
fee requirements. Section 15.12(e)(1) requires a permitted payment 
stablecoin issuer to publicly, clearly, and conspicuously disclose in 
plain language and in a format that is readily noticeable to payment 
stablecoin holders, and segregated from other information: the name of 
the permitted payment stablecoin issuer that issues the payment 
stablecoin; that the permitted payment stablecoin issuer is the entity 
that is obligated to convert, redeem, or repurchase the payment 
stablecoin for a fixed amount of monetary value; the website that 
contains a link to the monthly composition report of the relevant 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer's reserves required under Sec.  
15.11(e); all fees associated with purchasing or redeeming payment 
stablecoins; that the payment stablecoin is not legal tender, issued by 
the United States, or guaranteed or approved by the United States; and 
that payment stablecoins are not deposits, not backed by the full faith 
and credit of the United States, not subject to deposit insurance by 
the FDIC, and not subject to share insurance by the National Credit 
Union Administration. Additionally, Sec.  15.12(e)(2) requires the 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer to update the disclosures in Sec.  
15.12(e)(1)(iv) if there are any changes in fees associated with 
purchasing or redeeming payment stablecoins and provide payment 
stablecoin holders at least seven calendar days' prior notice of the 
change, including by delivering the notice to customers with whom the 
permitted payment stablecoin issuer has a current relationship. Section 
15.12(e)(3) also requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to 
publish the disclosures in Sec.  15.12(e)(1) and any updates made in 
accordance with Sec.  15.12(e)(2) on the permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer's website. Section 15.12(e)(4) also requires the permitted 
payment stablecoin issuer to include the disclosures in Sec.  
15.12(e)(1) and any updates made in accordance with Sec.  15.12(e)(2) 
in any customer agreements.
    Section 15.14(l) requires that the described annual financial 
statement includes the disclosure of any related party transactions, as 
defined by GAAP.
    Section 15.14(l)(2)(i) requires a permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer to make the audited financial statements under Sec.  
15.15(14)(l), publicly available on the permitted payment stablecoin 
issuer's website.
    Section 15.22(b) provides that a covered custodian may, for 
convenience, commingle the covered assets of multiple covered customers 
in one or more omnibus accounts to the extent that the steps it has 
taken pursuant to Sec.  15.21(b) are adequate to maintain safe and 
sound practices for the use and terms of any omnibus account, and to 
the extent that the use of omnibus accounts is consistent with 
applicable law, and is fully disclosed in the applicable custody 
agreement.
    Section 15.32(e) sets forth the conditions of approval for foreign 
payment stablecoin issuers seeking to be registered with the OCC under 
section 18(c) of the GENIUS Act (12 U.S.C. 5916(c)). Sections 
15.32(e)(1) and (2) provide that upon request by the OCC, foreign 
payment stablecoin issuers are required to grant the OCC prompt and 
complete access to all officers, directors, employees, and agents and 
to all relevant books, records, or documents of any type, in a form and 
location accessible to the OCC in the United States. The foreign 
payment stablecoin issuer is also required to make all information 
available to the OCC in English.
Estimated Burden
    Frequency: Weekly, monthly, quarterly, annually, event-generated, 
and on occasion.
    Respondents: National banks, Federal savings associations, Federal 
qualified payment stablecoin issuers, State qualified payment
